ChatGPT said:

Exactly. And that means we need to be careful not to turn a Bunsen shortcut into a Bench Monkey rule.

Bunsen’s ear happens to give us useful symmetry. A human body absolutely does not give us reliable perfect symmetry—nor will many handmade objects. Even two knitted ears that were supposed to match may have differences we want to preserve.

So Mirror is a construction tool, not an assumption.

Bench Monkey should never decide, “Oh, that's the left side, therefore I'll generate the right side.” You decide when something is symmetrical enough that mirroring saves work.

That actually makes the design cleaner: select any pins/lines → Duplicate → optionally Mirror or Rotate → position it → then the copy becomes ordinary editable geometry. Nothing remains permanently linked unless we deliberately add that capability someday.

For Bunsen: hell yes, exploit the symmetry. 😂

For a human: place the actual landmarks and follow the actual shape. If there's a portion where mirroring gives you a useful starting point, you can use it—but then break away and edit it independently.

So the underlying rule becomes:

Bench Monkey provides symmetry. It never presumes symmetry.

That one I really like. 🍌
